sections.description:
Short title extent and commencement

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
1. Short title, extent and commencement.‑(1) This
Ordinance may be called the West Pakistan Industrial Disputes Ordinance, 1968.
(2) It extends to the whole of
the Province of West Pakistan, except the Tribal Areas.
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

Definitions

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
2. Definitions.‑In this Ordinance, unless the context otherwise
requires, the following expressions shall have the meanings hereby respectively
assigned to them, that is to say‑
(a) "award" means the
determination by an Industrial Court of any industrial dispute or any matter
relating thereto, or any matter referred to it under clause (b) of subsection
(1) of section 11, and includes an interim award;
(b) "conciliation
officer" means a conciliation officer appointed under section 5;
(c) "conciliation proceeding" means any
proceeding held by a conciliation officer;
(d) "Court" means an Industrial Court
constituted under this ordinance;
(e) "Director" means
the Director of Labour Welfare, West Pakistan ;
(f) "employer"
includes‑
(i) in relation to an industry carried on by or under
the authority of any department of Government, the authority prescribed in this
behalf, or where no authority is prescribed, the head of the department;
(ii) in relation to an industry carried on by or on
behalf of a local authority, the chief executive officer of that authority; and
(iii) in relation to any other industry, the
proprietor of such industry and every director, manager, secretary, agent or
other officer or person concerned with the management thereof;
(g) "Government"
means the Government of West Pakistan;
(h) "industry" means, any business, trade,
undertaking, manufacture or calling of employers, and includes any calling,
service, employment,., handicraft, or industrial occupation or avocation of
workman.
(i) "industrial dispute" means any dispute
or difference between employers and employers, or between employers and
workmen, or between workmen and workmen, which is connected with the employment
or non‑ employment or the terms of employment or with the conditions of
work. of any person;
(j) "industrial establishment" shall have
the meaning assigned to it in: clause (f ) of section 2 of the West Pakistan
Industrial and Commercial Employment (Standing Orders) Ordinance, 1968;
(k) "Inspector" means
an Inspector appointed under section 4;
(1) "lock‑out" means the closing of a
place of employment or part of such place, or the suspension, wholly or partly,
of work by an employer, or refusal, absolute or conditional, by an employer to
continue to employ any number of persons employed by him, where such closing,
suspension or refusal occurs in connection with an industrial dispute, or is
intended for the purpose of compelling persons employed to accept certain term.
or conditions of, or affecting, employment;
(m) "member" means a
member of a Court;
(n) "prescribed"
means prescribed by rules made under this Ordinance;:
(o) "public utility
service" means‑
(i) any railway service;
(ii) any section of an industrial establishment, on
the working of which the safety of the establishment or the workmen employed
therein depends;
(iii) any postal, telegraph or
telephone service;
(iv) any industry which
supplies power, light or water to the public;
(v) any system of public
conservancy or sanitation;
(vi) any undertaking, establishment or installation
relating to the: defence services;
(vii) any service incidental to the maintenance of
naval dockyards or stores;
(viii) any service incidental to the maintenance and
operation of the port of Karachi, or of any other port in West Pakistan which
Government may; by notification in the official Gazette, declare to be a port
for the purposes of this Ordinance;
(ix) any transport by
mechanically propelled vehicle including aircraft;
(x) any service incidental to the maintenance and
operation of the Pakistan Security Printing Corporation;
(xi) any factory as defined in clause (j ) of section
2 of the Factories Act, 1934 (XXV of 1934), and engaged in the manufacture or
processing of such goods or commodities as are for the time being specified in
Part I. of the First Schedule;
(xii) any mine as defined in clause

Works committee

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
3. Works
Committee.‑(1) In the case of any industrial establishment. in which
fifty or more workmen are employed or have been employed on any day in the
preceding twelve months, the employer shall constitute in the prescribed manner
a Works Committee consisting of representatives of employers and workmen
engaged in the establishment so however that the number of representatives of
workmen on the Committee shall not be less than the number of representatives
of the employer.
(2) The representatives of the workmen shall be
chosen in the prescribed manner from among the workmen engaged in the
establishment and in consultation with their registered Trade Union, if any.
(3) The Works Committee shall promote measures for
securing and preserving amity and good relations between the employer and the
workmen and, to that end, comment upon matters of their common interest or
concern and endeavour to compose any material difference of opinion in respect
of such matters.

Inspectors and their duties

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
4. Inspectors
and their duties.‑(1) Government may, by notification in the official
Gazette, appoint such number of persons as it thinks tit. to be Inspectors for
the purpose of this Ordinance, and may specify the areas in which, or the
industries in respect of which, they may exercise their powers and perform
their functions under this Ordinance.
(2) Subject to any rules framed under section 44, an
Inspector appointed under this section‑-
(a) may
investigate any matter pertaining (to the constitution and proper functioning
of any Works Committee;
(b) after giving reasonable notice to the person in
charge of the premises, may enter any premises occupied by any establishment
for which a Works Committee has been constituted, for the purpose of performing
any functions imposed upon him by or under this Ordinance or the rules framed
thereunder.

Conciliation officers

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
5. Conciliation officers.‑(I) Government may, by notification
in the official Gazette, appoint such number of persons as it thinks fit, to be
conciliation officers for mediating in and promoting the settlement of
industrial disputes.
(2) A conciliation officer may
be appointed for a specified area or for specified industries in a specified
area or for one or more specified industries and either permanently or‑for
a limited period.

Duties of conciliation officers

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
6. Duties of conciliation officers.‑(I) Where any industrial
dispute exists or is apprehended in a public utility service, the conciliation
officer shall hold conciliation proceedings in the prescribed manner.
(2) Where any industrial
dispute not falling in subsection (I) exists or is apprehended, the
conciliation officer may, and shall, where a notice of strike has been
received, subject to the provisions of subsection (3), hold conciliation
proceedings in the prescribed manner.
(3) Where a notice of strike, whether in a public
utility service or in any other industry, has been received by the conciliation
officer, he shall satisfy himself as to its validity, and if the notice of strike
does not conform to the provisions of this Ordinance and the rules framed
thereunder, the said notice of strike shall not be deemed to have been given
under the provisions of this Ordinance and the conciliation officer may, in his
discretion, decide not to hold conciliation proceedings.
(4) Notwithstanding anything contained in subsection
(3), the validity of any conciliation proceedings shall not be called in
question on the ground that the notice of strike on receipt of which the
proceedings were initiated, did not conform to the provisions of this Ordinance
or the rules framed thereunder, or was otherwise invalid.
(5) The conciliation officer shall, for the purposes
of bringing about a settlement of the dispute, without delay investigate the
dispute and all matters affecting the merits and settlement thereof and may do
all such thing% as he thinks fit for the purpose of inducing the parties to come to a fair and amicable settlement
of the dispute.
(6) If a
settlement of the dispute or of any
matter in dispute is arrived at in the course of the conciliation proceedings, the conciliation officer shall
send a report thereof to Government together with a memorandum of the
settlement signed by the parties to the dispute.
(7) If no such settlement is arrived
at, in the case of a public utility service within fourteen days, and in any
other case within twenty‑eight days, of the commencement of the
conciliation proceedings, the conciliation officer shall, within seven days of
the close of the said period, issue a certificate to the parties to that
effect:
Provided that the period of
canciliation proceedings may be extended by mutual consent of the parties to
the dispute:
Provided further that the
conciliation officer may, in special circum stances to be recorded in writing,
issue a certificate of failure of the conciliation proceedings before the close
of the said period.
(8) Any party to whom a
certificate has been issued under sub section (7) may make an application,
within thirty days of its issue, to a Court for adjudication and determination
of the industrial dispute or of any matter constituting such dispute, and if no
such application is made within the said period, the dispute shall be deemed to
have ceased to exist;
Provided that in the case of an
industrial dispute to which the Central Government or the Provincial Government
is a party, no such application shall be made with respect to the dispute or
any matter constituting the dispute, if within twenty‑one days of the
issue of the certificate, Government, by an order published in the official
Gazette, declares that such dispute or matter is frivolous or vexatious or that
reference of such dispute or matter to the Court is inexpedient on public
grounds.

Procedure and powers of conciliation officers

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
7. Procedure and powers of conciliation officers.‑(1) The
conciliation officer shall, subject to the provisions of this Ordinance, follow
such procedure as may be prescribed.
(2) A conciliation officer may,
for the purpose of inquiry into any existing or apprehended industrial dispute
or for bringing about a settlement of such dispute‑---
(i) call for and inspect any
document which he has reason to believe to be relevant to the dispute;
(ii) convene a meeting of the
parties to the dispute; and
(iii) after: giving reasonable
notice to the person in charge of the premises or establishment, enter the
premises occupied by any establishment to which the dispute relates and do all
acts which he is required or empowered to do under this Ordinance.

Constitution of industrial Courts

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
8. Constitution of Industrial Courts.‑(1) Government may, for
adjudicating and determining any industrial disputes or any matter appearing to
be connected with or relevant to such disputes, by notification in the official
Gazette, constitute one or more Industrial Courts for such industries or areas
as may be specified therein.
(2) An Industrial Court shall
consist of a Chairman and two members to advise the Chairman, one of the members
to represent the employers .and the other to represent the workmen, all being
appointed by Govern ment.
(3) The Chairman shall be a person who is or has been
a District Judge or an Additional District Judge, and shall be appointed on
such terms and conditions as Government may determine.
(4) The members shall be appointed for a period of
one year in consultation with the employers and workmen in such manner as may
be prescribed and shall, on the expiry of the said period, be eligible for re‑appointment
for a further period not exceeding one year.
(5) If a member is absent from
any sitting of the Court or is otherwise incapable to sit as a member, the
Court may function in the absence of such member, and no act, proceeding,
decision or award of a Court shall be invalid merely by reason of absence of
any such member from any sitting of the Court.

Resignation removal and disqualification of members

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
9. Resignation,
removal and disqualification of members.‑(1) A member may resign his
office by a letter addressed to the Chairman and shall be deemed to have
vacated his office if he‑--
(i) is absent for a period of more than one month
from the sittings of the Court without leave of absence from the Chairman;
(ii) is adjudicated insolvent;
(iii) is convicted of an offence which, in the
opinion of Government, involves moral turpitude.
(2) If, in the opinion of Government, a member ceases
to be truly representative of those he was appointed to represent, Government
may forthwith remove him from his office.

Filling of casual vacancy

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
10. Filling of
casual vacancy.‑(1) If the office of the Chairman or of a member falls vacant or the
services of the Chairman otherwise cease to be available, Government shall fill
the vacancy in the manner laid down in section 8, and the proceedings shall be
continued before the Court with the Chairman or member so appointed.
(2) A member appointed to fill
a casual vacancy under subsection (1) shall hold office for the un-expired period
of the term of his predecessor.

Functions of the Court

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
11. Functions
of the Court.‑(1) The Court shall‑--
(a) adjudicate and determine
any industrial dispute in respect of which an application has been made to it
under subsection (8) of section 6;
(b) enquire into and adjudicate
any matter referred to it by Government for enquiry and adjudication;
(c) try offences under sections
33 and 35; and
(d) exercise and perform such other powers and
functions as are or may be conferred or imposed upon it by or under this
Ordinance.
(2) The Court may, at any stage of the proceedings
under clause (a) of subsection (1),
determine in a summary way the objections raised by any party to the dispute:
Provided that the party against whom an application
has been made under subsection (8) of section 6 shall raise at the first
hearing, all objections by his pleadings which snow the application to be not
maintainable on all such grounds of defence as, if not raised, would be likely
to take the opposite‑party by surprise or would raise new issues of facts
or law.
(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in the
Workmen's Compen sation Act, 1923 (VIII of 1923), the West Pakistan Industrial
and ‑Commercial Employment (Standing Orders) Ordinance, 1968, and the Payment
of Wages Act, 1936 (IV of 1936), Government may, by notification in the
official Gazette, appoint the Court to be or confer or impose upon it any
powers or functions of any authority under any of the said Acts or Ordinance,
and upon such notification, the Court shall be deemed to he such authority and
shall exercise the powers and perform the ;functions of such authority under
the relevant Act or Ordinance.

Procedure and powers of the Courts

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
12. Procedure and powers of the Courts.‑(1) The Court shall,
subject ,o the provisions of, this Ordinance, follow such procedure as may be
prescribed.
(2) The Court shall, for the purpose
of adjudicating and determining any industrial dispute, be deemed to be a Civil
Court and shall have the same powers as are vested in such Court under the Code
of Civil Procedure, 1908 (V of 1908), including the powers of‑---
(a) enforcing the attendance of
any person and examining him on oath;
(b) compelling the production of documents and
material objects; and
(c) issuing commissions for the
examination of witnesses.
(3) The Court shall, for the purposes of trying an
offence under section 33 or section 35, have the same powers as that of a Court
of the Magistrate of the first class under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898
(V of 1898), and shall, for the purpose of appeal from a sentence passed by it,
be deemed to be a Court of Session under that Code.
(4) No Court‑fee shall be
payable for filing, exhibiting, recording or obtaining of any document of any
kind in or from the Court.

Summoning of Amicus Curiae

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
13. Summoning
of amicus
curiae.‑(1) The Court shall have the power to summon any person
having necessary technical, professional or special knowledge to assist it in
connection with any matter pending before it.
(2) A person summoned under the
provisions of subsection (1) shall be paid such fees or honoraria as may be
prescribed.

Contempt of Court

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
14. Contempt
of Court.‑(I) Any person, who‑
(a) intentionally creates a
disturbance in or near any place in which this Court is sitting;
(b) wilfully interrupts the
proceedings of the Court;
(c) wilfully insults the
Chairman or a member of the Court when exercising the powers or performing
duties under this Ordinance;
(d) publishes or propagates any
defamatory .statement against the Chairman or a member as such;
shall be punishable by the Court with fine not
exceeding five hundred rupees, or with simple imprisonment for a term not
exceeding one month, o‑r with both.
(2) Any person convicted and
sentenced by the Court under sub section (1) to imprisonment for any period, or
to pay a fine exceeding fifty rupees, may prefer an appeal to the Tribunal, and
the Tribunal shall; when hearing such appeal, exercise all or any of the powers
conferred upon an appellate Court by section 423 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1898 (V of 1898).
sections.punishment:
punishable by the Court with fine not
exceeding five hundred rupees, or with simple imprisonment for a term not
exceeding one month, o‑r with both.

sections.description:
Procedure regarding decisions and awards of the Courts

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
15. Procedure
regarding decisions and awards of the Court.‑(1) The decisions of the Court under
section 26 or section 37, and the awards of the Court, shall be given in
writing signed by the Chairman, and‑--
(a) where the Central Government or the Provincial Government is a
party to the industrial disputes, two copies thereof shall immediately be
forwarded to Government; and
(b) in other cases, announced
in Court and two copies thereof forwarded to the Director.
(2) The award shall specify the period within which,
and where necessary, the parties or persons by whom, the award or any part
thereof shall be implemented:
Provided that where the Central or a Provincial
Government is a party, such period shall be fixed, in consultation with all the
parties to the dispute.
(3) Government shall, within a period of one month
from the date of receipt of an award or a decision of the Court under clause (a) of sub section (1), publish it in the
official Gazette, unless it is of opinion that it would be inexpedient on
public grounds to give effect to the whole or any part of the award.
(4) Where Government does not publish an award under
subsection (3), it shall, at the first available opportunity, lay the award
together with a statement of reasons for not so publishing it, before the
Provincial Assembly, and shall, as soon as may be, cause to be moved therein a
resolution for the consideration of the award, and the Provincial Assembly may,
by resolution, confirm, modify or reject the award.
(5) Unless
the award is rejected under subsection (4), Government shall, within one month
of its confirmation or modification by the Provincial' Assembly, publish it in
the official Gazette as so confirmed or modified.
(6) The decision of the Court on any other matter
that may come before it or be referred to it shall be dealt with in such manner
as may be prescribed.

Appeal

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
16. Appeal.‑(1) An appeal shall lie to the Tribunal‑-
-
(a) against an award given under clause (b) of subsection (1) of section 15, within thirty days of the
announcement of the award;
(b) against an award published under subsection (3) of section 15,
within thirty days of the publication of the award;
(c) against a decision of the Court under section 26
or section 37, within thirty days of the announcement of the decision under clause
(b) of sub section (l) of section 15, or its publication under subsection (3)
of that section, as the case may be;
and the decision of the
Tribunal in such appeal shall be final, and shall not be questioned in any
manner by or before any judicial or other authority, including the High Court.
(2) An award under subsection (5) of section 15, and
any decision of the Court other than an award or a decision under section 26 or
section 37, shall he final and shall not be questioned in any manner by or before
any judicial authority, including the High Court.

Constitution powers and procedure of tribunal

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
17. Constitution, powers and procedure of Tribunal.‑(1) The
Tribunal shall consist of one member to be appointed by Government by
notification in the official Gazette.
(2) The member of the Tribunal shall be a person who
is, or has been, or is qualified to be appointed as, a Judge of a High Court,
and shall be appointed on such terms and conditions as Government may
determine.
(3) The Tribunal may, on
appeal, confirm, set aside, vary or modify the award, sad shall exercise all
the powers conferred by this Ordinance on the Court, save as otherwise
provided.
(4) The Tribunal shall follow
such procedure as may be prescribed,
(5) Any person who‑
(a) intentionally
creates a disturbance in or near any place in which the Tribunal is sitting;
(b) wilfully interrupts
the proceedings of the Tribunal;
(c) wilfully insults
the member of the Tribunal when exercising the powers or performing his duties
under this Ordinance;
(d) publishes any defamatory statement against the
member of the Tribunal as such;
shall be punishable by the Tribunal with fine not
exceeding five hundred rupees, or with simple imprisonment for a term not
exceeding one month, or with both.
(6) Any person convicted and sentenced by the
Tribunal under sub section (5) to imprisonment for any period, or to pay a fine
exceeding fifty rupees, may prefer an appeal to the High Court.
sections.punishment:
punishable by the Tribunal with fine not
exceeding five hundred rupees, or with simple imprisonment for a term not
exceeding one month, or with both.

sections.description:
Persons on whom settlements and awards are binding

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
18. Persons on whom settlements and awards are binding.‑(1) A--- settlement
arrived at in the course of conciliation
proceedings or an award announced under clause (b) of subsection (1) of section
15 or published under subsection (3) or subsection (5) of that section shall be binding on‑--
(a) all parties to the industrial dispute:
(b) all other parties summoned to appear in the proceedings as
parties to the dispute, unless the Court records the opinion that they were so
summoned without proper cause;
(c) where a party referred to
in clause (b) is an employer, his
heirs, successors or assignees in respect of the establishment to which the
dispute relates;
(d) where a party referred to in clause (a) of clause (b) is composed of workmen, all persons who were employed in the
establishment or part. of the establishment, as the case may be, to which the
dispute relates on the date of the dispute and all persona who subsequently
become employed in that establishment or part thereof.
(2) A settlement arrived at by such agreement between
the employer and the workmen, as is referred to in clause (q) of section 2,
shall be binding on the parties to the
agreement.

Period of operation of settlements and awards

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
19. Period of operation of settlements and awards.‑(1) A settlement
shall come into operation on such date as is agreed upon by the parties to the
dispute, and if no date is agreed upon, on the date on which the memorandum of
the settlement is signed by the parties to the dispute.
(2) Such settlement shall be
building for such period as is agreed upon by the parties, and if no such
period is agreed upon, for a period of two
years from the date on which the memorandum of settlement is signed by
the parties to the dispute and shall continue to be binding on the parties
after the expiry of the period aforesaid, until the expiry of two months from
the date on which a notice in writing of an intention to terminate the
settlement is given by one of the parties to the other party or parties to the
settlement.
(3) An award given under clause
(b) of subsection (1) of section 15, unless it is appealed against to the
Tribunal, and an award published under subsection (3) of that section, shall
come into operation on such date and remain in operation for such period as may
be specified in the award:
Provided that before the expiry
of the said period, the Court may, upon an application of any party bound by
the award, by an order‑
(i) extend the period of
operation of the award by any period not exceeding one year at a time as it
thinks fit, so however, that the total period of operation of any award does
not exceed three years from the .date on which it came into operation; or
(ii) terminate the period of
the award so specified or extended, on a .date fixed by that order on the
ground of material change in the circum stances on which the award was based.
(4) An award published under
subsection (5) of section 15 shall come into operation on such date and remain
in operation for such period as may be specified in the award as confirmed or
modified by the Provincial Assembly.
(5) The decision of the
Tribunal in an appeal under subsection (1) of section 16 shall remain in
operation for such period, not exceeding one year, as may be specified in the
decision.
(6) Nothings contained in
subsection (3) shall apply to any award, nor ‑shall anything contained in
subsection (5) apply to a decision of the Tribunal in appeal, which by its
nature, terms or other circumstances, does ‑not impose, after it has been
given effect to, any continuing obligation on ‑the parties bound by the
award.
(7) Notwithstanding the expiry
of the period of operation under ,subsection (3), the award shall continue to
be binding on the parties until the expiry of two months from the date on which
a notice in writing of an intention to terminate the award is given by one of
the parties to the other party or parties to the award.

Consequences of failure to comply with the award

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
20. Consequences of failure to comply with the award.‑(1) Any
party or person required to comply with any settlement or award within a
specified period shall, within fourteen days of the elapse of that period,
report to the Director whether he has complied with the said settlement or
award.
(2) Where any party or person
referred to in subsection (1) has failed to comply with the direction in the
settlement or award, any person or party concerned may inform the Director to
that effect.
(3) If upon any information
received, under subsection (2) or otherwise, it appears to the Director or any
officer authorised by him in that behalf, that any party or person referred to
in subsection (1) has failed to comply with the settlement or award or any
direction contained therein, the Director or such other officer may make a
complaint to the Court, and thereupon the Court may proceed against the
defaulter under section 33 and give such further directions to secure the
implementation of the said settlement or award as it may deem fit.

Recovery of money from the employer under an award etc

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
21. Recovery of money from the employer under an award, etc.‑(1) Any
money due from an employer under any settlement, award, or decision of the
Court or the Tribunal, may be recovered as arrears of land‑revenue or as
a public demand by Government on an application made to it by or on behalf of
the person entitled to the money under the settlement, award or decision.
(2) Where any workman is
entitled to receive from the employer any benefit under an award or decision of
the Court or the Tribunal, which is capable of being computed in terms of
money, the amount at which such benefit should be computed may, subject to the
rules made under this Ordinance, be determined by that Court or the Tribunal,
as the case may he, and the amount so determined may be recovered as provided
for in subsection (1).

Commencement and conclusion of proceedings

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
22. Commencement
and conclusion of proceedings.‑(1) A conciliation proceeding shall be
deemed to have commenced----‑
(a) in the case of an
industrial dispute relating to a public utility service, where a notice of
strike or lock‑out under section 24 is given, on the date on which such
notice is received by the conciliation officer; and
(b) in other cases, on the date
on which the conciliation officer starts investigation under subsection (5) of
section 6.
(2) A conciliation proceeding shall be deemed to have concluded‑---
(a) where a
settlement is arrived at, when a memorandum of the settlement is signed by the
parties to the dispute; or
(b) where no settlement is arrived at, when a
certificate to that effect bas been issued under subsection (7) of section 6.
(3) Proceedings before a Court
shall be deemed to have commenced‑
(i) in relation to an industrial dispute, on the date
on which an application has been made under subsection (8) of section 6 for
adjudication, and
(ii) in relation to any other
matter, on the date it is referred to it, and such proceedings shall be deemed
to have concluded on the date on which the Court makes the award or gives its
decision.

Certain matters to be kept confidential

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
23. Certain matters to be kept
confidential.‑There shall not be included in any report, decision or
award under this Ordinance any information obtained by a conciliation officer,
Court or Tribunal in the course of any investigation or inquiry as to a Trade
Union or as to any individual business, whether carried on by a person, firm or
company, which is not available otherwise than through the evidence, given
before such officer, Court or Tribunal, if the Trade Union, person, firm or
company or question has made a request in writing to the conciliation officer,
Court or Tribunal that such information shall be treated as confidential nor
shall such conciliation officer or any person present at or concerned in the
proceedings disclose any such information without the consent in writing of the
Secretary of the Trade Union or the person, firm or company in question, as the
case may be:
Provided that nothing contained in this section shall
apply to a disclosure of any such information for the purposes of a prosecution
under section 193 of the Pakistan Penal Code (XLV of 1860).

Prohibition of strikes and lock outs in public utility service

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
24. Prohibition of strikes and lock‑outs in
public utility service.‑(1) No person employed in a public utility
service shall go on strike in breach of contract‑---
(a) without giving to the employer notice of strike,
as hereinafter provided, within six weeks before striking; or
(b) with fourteen days of
giving such notice; or
(c) before the expiry of the date of strike specified
in any such notice as aforesaid; or
(d) during the pendency of any conciliation
proceeding and, if no settlement is arrived at in the course of such
proceeding, before an application for adjudication of the dispute has been made
to the Court under subsection (8) of section 6.
(2) No employer carrying on any
public utility service shall lock‑out any of his workmen‑
(a) without giving them notice
of lock‑out, as hereinafter provided, within six weeks before locking‑out;
or
(b) within fourteen days of
giving such notice; or
(c) before the expiry of the
date of lock‑out specified in any such notice as aforesaid; or
(d) during the pendency of any conciliation
proceeding and, if no settlement is arrived at in the course of such
proceeding, before an appli cation for adjudication of the dispute has been
made to the Court under subsection (8) of section 6.
(3) The notice of lock‑out
or strike under this section shall not be necessary where there is already in
existence a strike or, as the case may be, lock‑out in the public utility
service, but the employer shall send intimation of such lock‑out or
strike on the day on which it is declared, to such authority as may be
specified by Government either generally or for a particular area or for a
particular class of public utility services.
(4) The notice of strike referred
to in subsection (l) shall be given by a registered Trade Union or by such
number of persons to such persons and in such manner as may be prescribed.
(5) The notice of lock‑out referred to in
subsection (2) shall be given in such manner as may be prescribed.
(6) If on any day an employer
receives from any persons employed by him or from a registered Trade Union any
such notices as are re erred to in subsection (1) or gives to any persons
employed by him any such notices as are referred to in subsection (2), he shall
within five days thereof report to Government or to such authority as
Government may prescribe the number and contents of such notices received or
given on that day.

General prohibition of strikes and lock-outs

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
25. General prohibition of
strikes and lock‑outs.‑No workman employed in any industrial
establishment shall go on strike and no employer of any such workman shall
declare a lock‑out‑---
(a) during the pendency of conciliation proceedings
before a conciliation officer and seven days after the conclusion of such
proceedings; or
(b) during the pendency of
proceedings before a Court; or
(c) during the pendency of any
appeal to the Tribunal under sub section (1) of section 16; or
(d) during any period in which a settlement or award is in
operation, In respect of any of the matters covered by the settlement or award.

Power of Court to prohibit strike or lock-out

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
26. Power of Court to prohibit strike or lock‑out.‑Where
a strike or lock out has already commenced and is in existence at the time of
the application to the Court under subsection (8) of section 6 for adjudication
of the dispute, or of the reference to the Court under clause (b) of sub section
(i) of section 1 I for inquiry into and adjudication of any matter, the Court
may, by order, prohibit the continuance of the strike or lock‑out.

Power of Government to prohibit strike or lock-out

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
27. Power of Government to prohibit strike or lock‑out.
‑Notwith standing anything contained elsewhere in this Ordinance to the
contrary, where a strike or lock‑out, in pursuance of an industrial
dispute, is apprehended or has already commenced and Government is satisfied
that it is necessary to prohibit such strike or lock‑out in the public
interest or for the maintenance of services or supplies essential to the
community, Government may at any time, by an order, published in the official
Gazette, prohibit such strike or lock‑out:
Provided that any order issued under this section
shall remain in force for a period not exceeding three months at a time from
the date of such order.

Illegal strike or lock-outs

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
28. Illegal strikes or lock‑outs.‑(I) A
strike or a lock‑out shall be illegal, if‑
(i) it is commenced or declared in contravention of
section 24 or section 25; or
(ii) it is continued in
contravention of an order made under section 26; or
(iii) it is commenced or continued in contravention
of an order made under section 27.
(2) A lock‑out declared in consequence of an
illegal strike or a strike declared in consequence of an illegal lock‑out
shall not be deemed to be illegal.

Prohibition of financial aid to illegal strikes and lock-outs

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
29. Prohibition of financial
aid to illegal strikes and lock‑outs.‑No
person shall knowingly expend or apply any money in direct furtherance or
support of any illegal strike or lock‑out.

Penalty for  illegal strikes and lock-outs

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
30. Penalty for
illegal strikes and lock‑outs.‑(1) Any workman who commences,
continues or otherwise acts in furtherance of a strike which is illegal under
this Ordinance, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may
extend to six months, or with a fine of one hundred rupees, or with both.
(2) Any employer who commences, continues or
otherwise acts in furtherance of a took‑out which is illegal under this
Ordinance, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to
six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both,
and in the case of a continuing offence with a further fine of one hundred
rupees for every day after the first during which the offence continues.
sections.punishment:
punishable with imprisonment for a term which may
extend to six months, or with a fine of one hundred rupees, or with both.

sections.description:
Penalty for instigations etc

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
31. Penalty for
instigations etc.‑Any person who instigates or incites others to take
part in, or otherwise acts in furtherance of, a strike or lock‑out which
is illegal under this Ordinance, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a
term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one
thousand rupees, or with both.
sections.punishment:
punishable with imprisonment for a
term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one
thousand rupees, or with both.

sections.description:
Penalty for giving financial aid to  illegal strikes and lock-outs

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
32. Penalty for giving financial aid to illegal strikes and lock‑outs‑Any
person who knowingly expends or applies any money in direct furtherance or
support of any illegal strike or lock‑out shall be punishable with
imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may
extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
sections.punishment:
punishable with
imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may
extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

sections.description:
Penalty for breach of settlement or award

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
33. Penalty for breach of
settlement or award.‑If any person commits a breach of any term of any
settlement or award which is binding on him under this Ordinance, be shall, on
conviction therefor, be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may
extend to six months, or with fine upto five hundred rupees, or with both, and
if the breach be a continuing one, with a further fine which may extend to two
hundred rupees for each day after the first during which such breach continues.
sections.punishment:
punishable with imprisonment for a term which may
extend to six months, or with fine upto five hundred rupees, or with both, and
if the breach be a continuing one, with a further fine which may extend to two
hundred rupees for each day after the first during which such breach continues.

sections.description:
Penalty for disclosing confidential information

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
34. Penalty for disclosing confidential information.‑Any
person who wilfully discloses any such information as is referred to in
section 23, in contravention of the provisions of that section shall, on
complaint made by or on behalf of the Trade Union or individual business
affected, be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six
months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
sections.punishment:
punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six
months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

sections.description:
Penalty for other offences

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
35. Penalty for other offences.‑(I)
Any employer who contravenes the provisions of section 37 shall be punishable
with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which
may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
(2) Whoever contravenes any of
the provisions of this Ordinance or any rule made thereunder shall, if no other
penalty is provided by or under this Ordinance for such contravention, be
punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees.
sections.punishment:
punishable
with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which
may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

sections.description:
Offences by companies etc

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
36. Offences by companies, etc.‑Where
a person committing an offence under this Ordinance is a company, or other body
corporate, or act association of persons, every director, manager, secretary,
agent or other officer or person concerned with the management thereof shall,
unless he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or
consent, be deemed to be guilty of such offence.

Conditions of services, etc., to remain unchanged during pendency of proceedings

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
37. Conditions of services
etc.. to remain unchanged during pendency of proceedings.‑(1) No employer
shall, during the pendency of conciliation proceedings or proceedings before a
Court or the Tribunal in respect of an industrial dispute or during the period
between the conclusion of the conciliation proceedings and the commencement of
the proceedings before the Court, alter, to the prejudice of the workmen
concerned such dispute, the conditions of service applicable to them
immediately before the commencement of conciliation proceedings, nor shall he‑--
(a) save with the permission of the conciliation
officer, during the pendency of conciliation proceedings and the period
thereafter preceding the commencement of the proceedings before the Court, and
(b) save with the permission of
the Court, during the pendency of the proceedings before the Court, and of the
Tribunal during the pendency of proceedings before it discharge, dismiss or otherwise
punish any such workmen except for misconduct not connected with such dispute.
(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in subsection
(1)‑-- (a) an officer of a registered Trade Union shall not, during the
pendency of any proceedings or period specified in that subsection, be
discharged or dismissed for misconduct not connected with the dispute referred
to therein, except with the permission of the Court, but he may, pending the
disposal of an application to the Court for such permission, be placed under
suspension, provided that during the period of suspension he shall be paid
fifty per centum of his wages as subsistence allowance;
(b) a workman who has completed
service of nine months shall not, during the pendency of any proceedings or
period referred to in hub‑ section (1), be discharged or dismissed for
misconduct not connected with the dispute, except in accordance with the
provisions of the West Pakistan Industrial and Commercial Employment (Standing
Orders) Ordinance, 1968, applicable to such workman, and unless he has been
paid wages for a period of one month following such discharge or dismissal and
an, application is made within seven days of such action to the authority
before which the proceeding is pending for approval of the action taken by the
employer:
Provided that where the
authority to which the application for approval is made disapproves of such
action, the workman shall be re‑instated by the employer:
Provided further that the rate
of subsistence allowance admissible
under this subsection shall not apply to any industry run by or under the:
authority of the Central or the Provincial Government to which any specific or general rules on the
subject are applicable:
Provided also that for the purposes of clause (b),
the provisions of the West Pakistan Industrial and Commercial Employment
(Standing Orders) Ordinance, 1968, shall not apply to any workman in an
industry run by or under the authority of the Central or the Provincial
Government to which,. specific or general rules or procedure for dismissal or
discharge of workmen are applicable.
(3) The Court shall deal with
an application under subsection (2) in
such summary way as it may think fit.
Explanation.‑In
this section "an officer of a registered Trade Union" has the
same meaning as in the West Pakistan Trade Unions Ordinance, 1968.

Special provision for adjudication in the case of contravention of section 37

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
38. Special
provision for adjudication in the case of contravention of section 37.‑Where an employer
contravenes the provisions of section 37 during the pendency of proceedings
before a Court, any workman aggrieved by such contravention may make a
complaint in writing in the prescribed manner to such Court and on receipt of
such complaint, that Court shall adjudicate upon the complaint as if it were an
industrial dispute in respect of which application has been made under
subsection (8) of section 6.

Cognizance of offences

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
39. Cognizance of offences.‑(1)
No Court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this
Ordinance or of the abetment of any
such offence, save on complaint made by or under the authority of
Government.
(2) No Court inferior to that of a Magistrate of the
first class shall try any offence punishable under this Ordinance.
(3) Nothing in this section shall apply to a Court
constituted under this Ordinance which shall have exclusive jurisdiction to try
offences under section 33 and subsection (1) of section 35 on complaint made by the Director or an officer authorised by
him in this behalf, or the aggrieved` person or party.
sections.punishment:
punishable under this
Ordinance or of the abetment of any
such offence, save on complaint made by or under the authority of
Government.

sections.description:
Protection of persons

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
40. Protection
of persons.‑(1) No person refusing to take part or to continue to
take part in any strike or lock‑out which is illegal under this Ordinance
shall, by, reason of such refusal or by reason of any action taken by him under
this section, be subject to expulsion from any Trade Union or to any fine or
penalty or to deprivation of any right or benefit to which he or his legal
representatives would otherwise be entitled, or be liable to be placed in any
respect, either directly or indirectly, under any disability or at any
disadvantage as compared with other members of Union, anything to the contrary
in the rules of a Trade Union notwithstanding.
(2) Nothing in the rules of a Trade Union requiring
the settlement .of disputes in any manner shall apply to any proceeding for
enforcing any right or exemption secured by this section, and in any such
proceedings the Civil Court may, in lieu of ordering a person who has been expelled
from membership of a Trade Union to be restored to membership, order that he be
paid out of the funds of the Trade Union such sum by way of compensation or
damages as that Court thinks just.

Representation of parties

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
41.
Representation of parties.‑(1) No party to an industrial dispute ‑shall
be entitled to be represented by a legal practitioner‑
(a) in any conciliation proceedings; or
(b) in any proceedings before a Court adjudicating
such dispute, except with the consent of all the parties to the dispute and the
approval of the Court.
(2) Subject
to the provisions contained in subsection (1), a workman or an employer who is
a party to an industrial dispute shall be entitled to be represented in any
proceedings under this Ordinance by an officer of a Trade Union or Federation
of workmen or employers registered under the West Pakistan Trade Unions
Ordinance, 19 8, as the case may be.

Interpretation of settlements and awards

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
42.
Interpretation of settlements and awards.‑(1) If any difficulty or
doubt arises as to the interpretation of any provisions of an award or
settlement, it shall be referred to a Court constituted under this Ordinance.
(2) The Court to which a matter is referred under
subsection (1) shall, after giving the parties an opportunity of being heard,
decide the matter, and its decision shall be final and binding on the parties.

Protection of action taken under the ordinance

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
43. Protection
of action taken under the Ordinance.‑No suit, prosecution or other
legal proceedings, shall lie against any person for anything which is in good
faith done or intended to be done in pursuance of this Ordinance or any rules
framed thereunder.

Power to make rules

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
44. Power to make rules.‑(I) Government may, subject to the
condition of previous publication, make rules for carrying out the purposes of
this Ordinance.
(2) In particular and without
prejudice to the generality of the ‑foregoing power, such rules may
provide for all or any of the following matters, namely:‑
(a) the powers and procedure of
conciliation officers, Courts and the Tribunal, including rules as to the
summoning of witnesses, the production of documents relevant to the subject‑matter
of an inquiry or investigation, and the manner of submission of reports,
decisions and awards;
(b) the constitution and functions of, and the
filling of vacancies in, Works Committees, and the procedure to be followed by
such Committees in the discharge of their duties;
(c) the powers of Inspectors
and the Director;
(d) the allowances admissible
to the amicus curie and witnesses ;
(e) the ministerial establishments which may be allotted to a Court
and Tribunal, and the salaries and allowances payable to such estab lishments;
(f ) the manner in which, and the persons by and to whom, notice of
strike or lock‑out may be given, and the manner in which such notices
shall be communicated; and
(g) any other matter which is
to be or may be prescribed.

Power to Government to change schedules

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
45. Power of Government
to change Schedules.‑Government may, by notification in the official
Gazette, add to or exclude from the
Schedules any goods, commodity or industry.

Repeal and savings

ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
ORDINANCE IV OF 1968
WEST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTES ORDINANCE, 1968
46. Repeal and
savings. (I) The Industrial Disputes
Ordinance, 1959 . .VI of 1959), in its application to the Province of West
Pakistan, hereinafter referred to as the said Ordinance, is hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding the repeal of the said Ordinance,
anything done. rules, notifications or orders issued, officers appointed,
Courts constituted. notices given, references and applications to Courts made,
proceedings commenced or other action taken under the said Ordinance shall, so
far as the same are not inconsistent with the provisions of this Ordinance, be
continued and be deemed to have been respectively done, issued, appointed
constituted, given, made, commenced or taken under this Ordinance.
